findings.title: Blocklist lookup is case-sensitive, so a blocked address written with different letter case is not blocked
findings.description: `should_block?` runs `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` on the raw value. Nothing normalizes it on the way in. `User.new_from_params` stores `params[:email]` unchanged (app/models/user.rb:84-91), and `EmailValidator#validate_each` passes the raw `value` through (lib/validators/email_validator.rb:13). The app uses PostgreSQL (Gemfile `pg`; config/database.yml.*-sample `adapter: postgresql`), where `=` is case-sensitive. A stored entry `bad@spamclub.com` therefore does not match a signup for `BAD@spamclub.com`, so changing the case of the local part gets past the block. The domain checks in the same validator match case-insensitively (`Regexp.new(..., true)`, email_validator.rb:20), so the new check is inconsistent with its neighbor. `Email.downcase` lowercases only the domain (lib/email.rb:19-22), so the fix has to downcase the whole address on both write and lookup.

findings.title: Each signup attempt adds two to a blocked email's match_count because the validator, with its side effect, runs twice
findings.description: `EmailValidator` calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?`, which increments `match_count` and sets `last_match_at` on every call (app/models/blocked_email.rb:13-16). Validation runs on every `valid?`. In `UsersController#create`, `user.valid?` runs at line 168 and `user.save` runs at line 172, and `save` validates again. `email_changed?` stays true between those calls, so the validator runs both times. One signup attempt with a blocked address therefore records two matches, and the counters overstate the real number. Recording the match once, outside validation, would fix it.

findings.title: Redeeming an invite for a blocked address raises an unhandled RecordInvalid, so the invite fails with a server error
findings.description: Invite creation never checks the blocklist. `Invite` validates only presence, `invited_by_id`, and that no user exists with the address (app/models/invite.rb:12-33), so an invite for a blocked address can be created. On redemption, `InviteRedeemer#create_new_user` calls `User.create_for_email` (app/models/invite_redeemer.rb:46-47), which calls `user.save!` (user.rb:103). The new blocklist check fails validation, `save!` raises `ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid`, and nothing rescues it. `InvitesController#show` calls `invite.redeem` with no rescue (invites_controller.rb:12). `ApplicationController`'s `rescue_from Exception` logs the error and re-raises it (application_controller.rb:38-48), so the invitee gets a server error. The transaction in `InviteRedeemer#redeem` rolls back `redeemed_at`, so the invite stays unredeemed and the same error repeats on every visit. The same unhandled path already exists for whitelist and blacklisted domains. This change adds blocked addresses as another trigger.

findings.title: Concurrent matches on the same blocked entry can lose match_count increments
findings.description: `record.match_count += 1` followed by `record.save` is a read-modify-write in Ruby. Two signups that match the same entry at the same moment can both read N and both save N+1, which loses one match. Only the counter and `last_match_at` are affected; the block decision is not. An atomic `update_counters` would avoid this.
